hints.title: Circular Neighborhood Conflict Obstacle
hints.text: Because houses are arranged in a circle, robbing the first house excludes robbing the last house. How can decomposing the circular street into two independent linear segments eliminate the wrap-around dependency?

hints.title: Boundary Exclusion Bipartition Invariant
hints.text: The optimal loot is the maximum of two independent subproblems: robbing houses from index 0 to n - 2, or robbing houses from index 1 to n - 1.

hints.title: Linear Subproblem Evaluation Procedure
hints.text: Handle cases where length is at most 2 directly. Define a helper that runs the standard linear non-adjacent robber algorithm in O(1) space. Compute the helper result on the slice omitting the last house, compute it on the slice omitting the first house, and return the maximum of the two results.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of houses in circular street
complexity.notes: Runs two linear passes over N - 1 elements using constant auxiliary registers.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Exploring all valid non-adjacent subsets in a circle takes O(2^N) exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Splitting into two linear passes avoids complicated modular state transitions.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizing that circular adjacency simplifies into two linear subproblems.

solutions.approach: Circular problem decomposition into dual linear subproblems
